title: Staff Handbook
summary: How Pelagos operates and what is expected of every employee. Version 3.0 also includes the rules from the staff memos: breaks, clocking, pay, leave, public holidays, phones, uniform and hygiene.
body:
> **Please note:** This handbook must be read together with each employee’s signed employment contract and any lawful management instructions issued from time to time.
>
> **New in version 3.0:** The rules from the staff memos on hygiene, uniforms, pay, confidentiality, public holidays, cellphones, clocking, attendance, sick leave and breaks are now part of this handbook. Those memos have been withdrawn, and this handbook replaces them.

## 1. WELCOME TO PELAGOS

Welcome to Pelagos. We are a premium-casual restaurant built on quality, consistency and genuine hospitality. Every staff member contributes directly to the guest experience, the reputation of the business, and the culture of the team.

This handbook is written to help every employee understand how Pelagos operates, what standards are expected, and what support structures exist in the business. It does not replace your contract of employment. It works alongside your contract, company policies, lawful instructions from management, and the estate rules that apply to all staff working at Villa Del Mare.

### What this handbook is for

- To explain the standards of behaviour, service and hygiene expected at Pelagos.
- To give every employee one practical reference point for daily operations.
- To support fair, consistent management and onboarding across all departments.
- To protect the Pelagos brand, the safety of guests and staff, and the business itself.

## 2. BRAND CULTURE AND GUEST PROMISE

Pelagos is designed to feel polished without being stiff, family-oriented without being basic, and locally grounded while still meeting a high, professional standard. Our service tone is warm, confident and neighbourly. Guests must feel welcome, looked after and comfortable from the moment they arrive until the moment they leave.

### 2.1 Who we are

- **Welcoming:** every guest must feel received, not processed.
- **Polished:** standards must be neat, sharp and professional.
- **Family-oriented:** children are welcome and parents must feel at ease.
- **Reliable:** quality and service must be consistent every day.
- **Adaptable:** the team must respond professionally to different guest needs and different service periods.

### 2.2 Our guest promise

- **Quality without pretension:** excellent food and service without arrogance.
- A clean, safe and comfortable environment for guests of all ages.
- **Real hospitality:** not just delivering food, but delivering an experience.
- **Attention to detail:** the small things shape the overall impression of the restaurant.

## 3. EMPLOYMENT FRAMEWORK

Pelagos makes use of permanent, fixed-term, hourly and casual employment arrangements. The terms that apply to your role are recorded in your signed contract. All employees are required to comply with this handbook regardless of the type of contract under which they are employed.

### 3.1 Induction and probation

Every new employee must undergo induction before or immediately after starting work.

Induction includes an introduction to the premises, estate access rules, key policies, service standards and department procedures.

New front of house recruits first work a paid 6-day training contract: five training shifts (2 on the floor, 1 in the bar and 2 in the kitchen) and a written test on the sixth day. The pass mark is 80%. Recruits who do not pass are not appointed (see PEL-SOP-011 Staff Onboarding, section 3).

The standard probation period is three months unless a different term is recorded in the contract of employment.

During probation, attendance, conduct, suitability, work quality and trainability are assessed.

### 3.2 Job responsibilities

- Employees are employed for the role stated in their contract but may reasonably be instructed to perform related duties required by operations.
- Managers may adjust duties, shifts and responsibilities where business needs require it, provided this is reasonable and lawful.
- All employees are expected to attend training, receive feedback professionally and continuously improve their job knowledge.

## 4. ATTENDANCE, HOURS AND SCHEDULING

Pelagos is a hospitality operation. Business needs vary by season, service period, events and trading levels. Staff must therefore work to scheduled shifts and be ready for duty at the prescribed start time.

### 4.1 Working hours

- Ordinary hours are a maximum of 45 hours per week, subject to the employee’s contract and the law.
- Shift schedules are set by management to meet operational needs.
- Where allowed by the contract and the law, hours may be averaged over a defined cycle.
- Meal and rest breaks are set out in section 4.2.

### 4.2 Breaks

- **Meal break:** if you work a shift of 6 hours or more, you get one unpaid meal break of 30 minutes, as agreed in writing in your employment contract. Take it in one go, and start it before you have worked 5 hours without a break.
- **Rest breaks:** two paid rest breaks of 15 minutes each during your shift.
- **Smoke breaks:** smoke only during your rest breaks or meal break. No extra or separate breaks are given for smoking.

To keep enough staff on duty during peak trading, no breaks may be taken during these times:

| **Morning**    | **Lunch**      | **Dinner**     |
|----------------|----------------|----------------|
| 09:00 to 11:00 | 12:00 to 15:00 | 17:30 to 20:30 |

- **Plan your breaks:** agree your break times with your supervisor at the start of your shift, outside the restricted times.
- **Quiet periods:** if it is quiet and you would like to take your break, confirm with the Duty Manager first.
- **Rest properly:** step away from your workstation during your break.
- **Be on time:** return from your break on time, out of respect for your colleagues and to keep service running smoothly.

> **Note:** If your shift pattern makes it hard to start your meal break within your first 5 hours because of the restricted times, speak to the Duty Manager so that your break can be planned.

### 4.3 Punctuality and readiness

- Employees must arrive in time to be in full uniform and ready to work at the shift start time.
- Late arrival must be reported directly to the manager as soon as possible. Messages through colleagues are not acceptable unless there is an emergency.
- Repeated lateness, absenteeism or poor timekeeping may result in disciplinary action.

### 4.4 Clocking in and out

- All staff must clock in and out on the fingerprint scanner on the Pilot POS at every shift (in place since 18 May 2026).
- The Pilot record is the record used for payroll. It is your responsibility to make sure your attendance is captured correctly.

### How to clock in or out:

1.  **Find the scanner:** the fingerprint reader is on the side or base of the Pilot POS terminal.
2.  **Check the screen:** make sure the terminal is on the main login screen.
3.  **Scan your finger:** place your registered finger firmly and flat on the scanner.
4.  **Select the action:** once the system recognises you, select Clock In at the start of your shift or Clock Out at the end.
5.  **Wait for confirmation:** wait for the “Success” message to confirm your time has been captured.

### If the scanner fails or you forget to clock:

1.  Tell the Duty Manager immediately, during the same shift.
2.  The Duty Manager writes your actual time in or out in the back-up Manual Clocking Register (the Blue File at the kitchen entrance), and you both sign the entry.
3.  The Duty Manager corrects the record in Pilot on the same day (see PEL-SOP-004 Duty Manager Procedure).

> **No clock, no record:** A missed clock-in or clock-out that is not reported and corrected on the same day is recorded as “Not at Work” for that shift.

- **Clocking for someone else:** clocking in or out for another person, or asking someone to clock for you, is clocking fraud. This is gross misconduct under PEL-POL-002 Disciplinary Code and Probation Policy.
- **Your fingerprint:** your fingerprint is stored in Pilot and used only to record attendance for payroll, in line with POPIA. Before it is registered, you are asked to sign the Fingerprint Clocking Consent Form (PEL-FRM-002).
- **If you do not consent:** your times are written in the Manual Clocking Register at every shift and signed by you and the Duty Manager, who enters them in Pilot. Not giving consent does not affect your employment.

### 4.5 Absence from a rostered shift

- **Let us know early:** if you cannot come to work, contact your manager directly (not through a colleague) as early as possible before your shift starts.
- **Unpaid absence:** if you are rostered to work and do not come in, and the absence is not approved leave (annual leave, sick leave or family responsibility leave), the day is unpaid and is deducted from your pay.
- **Discipline:** absence without notice is a disciplinary offence under PEL-POL-002 Disciplinary Code and Probation Policy.
- Sick leave and medical certificates are covered in section 5.4.

### 4.6 Rosters, shift changes and short time

- Employees may not exchange shifts without management approval.
- Changes to the roster will be communicated by management. Staff are responsible for checking rosters and instructions.
- In periods of reduced trade, management may introduce short time or reduced hours where permitted by law and contract.

## 5. REMUNERATION, CONFIDENTIALITY AND LEAVE

### 5.1 Salary payment

Salaries are paid by EFT into the employee’s nominated bank account on the last day of each month. If the last day of the month falls on a weekend or public holiday, salaries are paid on the last working day before it.

- **Hourly-paid staff:** the monthly cut-off is the 20th. Each month’s pay covers the hours worked from the 21st of the previous month to the 20th of the current month. Hours worked after the 20th are paid in the following month.
- **Monthly salaried staff** are paid for the full calendar month (the 1st to the last day of the month).
- **New hourly staff:** your first pay covers the hours worked from your start date to the 20th of that month. If you start after the 20th, those hours are paid at the end of the next month.
- **New salaried staff:** your first pay is pro rata, from your start date to the last day of the month.
- The cut-off dates and paydays for each month are in the hourly pay calendar memo (PEL-MEM-015), which is issued each year.

### 5.2 Salary confidentiality and company information

- **Your own pay:** you may discuss your own salary and conditions of employment with anyone. This right is protected by section 78 of the Basic Conditions of Employment Act, and you will not be disciplined for it. If you have a question or concern about your pay, please speak to Management so that we can help.
- **Other people’s pay and personal information:** you may not share another employee’s salary, pay details or personal information that you see or hear through your work, for example their ID number, contact details, bank details, or disciplinary or medical information. Colleagues’ and guests’ personal information must be protected in line with the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA).
- **Company information:** as agreed in your employment contract, you must act in good faith towards Pelagos and keep company information confidential, including:
  - payroll and HR records;
  - financial information about the business;
  - supplier prices and agreements;
  - guest information and bookings; and
  - business plans and internal documents.
- Do not share any information that could benefit another party to the detriment of the business.

> **Important:** Breaking the rules on other people’s information or company information is serious misconduct and may lead to disciplinary action under PEL-POL-002 Disciplinary Code and Probation Policy.

### 5.3 Deductions and losses

- Statutory deductions such as tax and UIF will be made where applicable.
- Authorised deductions may be made for uniforms, protective clothing, approved loans or other agreed items.
- Where lawful and properly investigated, losses or damages caused by employee fault may result in deductions subject to legal limits.

### 5.4 Leave

- Annual leave, sick leave, family responsibility leave, parental leave and maternity leave are granted in line with the employee’s contract and the Basic Conditions of Employment Act (BCEA).
- All leave must be requested in advance where possible and approved by management.
- If you are ill or have an emergency, contact your manager directly (not through a colleague) as early as possible before your shift starts.

### Sick leave

- During your first 6 months of employment, you earn **1 day of paid sick leave for every 26 days you work**. Sick days taken beyond what you have earned are unpaid.
- After 6 months you move onto the BCEA sick leave cycle of 36 months. In each cycle you are entitled to the number of days you would normally work in 6 weeks: for example, 30 days if you normally work 5 days a week, or 36 days if you normally work 6 days a week.
- Paid sick leave taken during your first 6 months is subtracted from your first 36-month cycle.

### Medical certificates

A medical certificate is required for sick leave to be paid if:

- you are off sick for more than 2 consecutive days; or
- you have been off sick on more than 2 occasions in an 8-week period.

The certificate must be issued and signed by a registered medical practitioner (such as a doctor or a registered clinic nurse) and must state that you were unable to work.

### 5.5 Public holidays

Public holidays are some of our busiest days. Pay and time off for public holidays follow section 18 of the BCEA.

- **Rostering:** public holiday shifts are rostered in advance and worked by agreement, as set out in your employment contract. Your manager confirms the public holiday roster with you.
- **Hourly-paid staff who work on a public holiday** are paid double their normal hourly rate for every hour worked. For example, an 8-hour shift is paid as 16 hours.
- **Hourly-paid staff who are not rostered** on a public holiday that falls on a day they would normally work are still paid their normal wage for that day.
- **Fixed-term staff** follow the rule for hourly-paid or monthly salaried staff, depending on how they are paid.

**Monthly salaried staff:** your monthly salary already includes pay for public holidays you do not work. If you work on a public holiday, you have two options:

1.  **Double pay:** you are paid double your normal daily rate for the public holiday worked; or
2.  **Time off instead of pay:** if you agree in writing before the holiday, you earn double time back as paid time off. For example, an 8-hour public holiday shift earns 16 hours of paid time off, taken within 4 months of the holiday on dates agreed with management, normally in quieter trading periods.

If there is no written agreement for time off, option 1 (double pay) applies.

> **Attendance:** If you do not come to work for a rostered public holiday shift without a valid medical certificate, the day is unpaid and you may face disciplinary action.

If you have questions about your payslip or how your hours are tracked, please visit the administration office.

## 6. CONDUCT, COMMUNICATION AND WORKPLACE STANDARDS

Professional conduct is essential at Pelagos. Staff represent the brand at all times while on duty, on the estate and when dealing with guests, suppliers, management and fellow employees.

### 6.1 General conduct

- Treat guests, residents, suppliers and fellow employees with dignity and respect.
- Obey lawful and reasonable instructions from management.
- Do not perform private work or personal business during working time.
- Do not bring the business into disrepute through gossip, reckless talk or unprofessional behaviour.
- Do not consume alcohol or use drugs while on duty or report for duty under the influence.

### 6.2 Communication

- Speak clearly, respectfully and professionally at all times.
- Do not shout across the dining room, kitchen, bar or service areas.
- Do not discuss salaries, grievances, management decisions, private matters or staff conflict within earshot of guests.
- If you do not know the answer to a guest’s question, never say “I don’t know”; say “Let me find out for you.”

### 6.3 Personal mobile phones

- Personal cellphones may not be kept on your person while on duty, unless management authorises it for work purposes (for example the Duty Manager).
- **Check-in:** at the start of your shift, switch your phone to silent and store it in your locker, or hand it in at the Duty Manager’s office. It stays there until your break or the end of your shift. Phones handed in are kept locked in the Duty Manager’s office and returned to you at your break and at the end of your shift.
- **Breaks:** you may use your phone during your approved breaks, away from guest areas.
- **Emergencies:** family and others can reach you on the restaurant landline or through the Duty Manager. If you are expecting an urgent call, tell the Duty Manager at the start of your shift.
- **Working time is for work:** using your phone, or being idle when there are tasks to do, means work you are paid for is not being done.
- **Breaches** are dealt with under PEL-POL-002 Disciplinary Code and Probation Policy (verbal warning, then written warning, then final written warning).

### 6.4 Honesty and conflict of interest

- All employees are expected to act honestly at all times.
- Misconduct by colleagues, stock irregularities, theft, fraud or security concerns must be reported immediately.
- Employees must disclose outside business interests or secondary employment where there may be a conflict with Pelagos.

## 7. UNIFORM, GROOMING AND HYGIENE

Personal appearance and hygiene are essential to the Pelagos image and to food safety. Staff are expected to report for duty clean, neat, correctly dressed and fit for work.

### 7.1 Personal hygiene requirements

- Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and warm water before starting work, after breaks, after smoking, after using the toilet, after handling raw food and whenever contamination may have occurred. Use hand sanitiser only when soap and water are not available.
- Keep nails short and clean. Kitchen staff and anyone handling food may not wear nail polish or false nails. Front of house, bar, housekeeping and admin staff may wear nail polish if it is neat, with no chips, peeling or add-ons.
- Hair must be clean and well groomed. Long hair (shoulder length or longer) must be tied back or secured. Bar and restaurant staff must keep their hair neat and away from food and drinks.
- Kitchen staff must wear a hairnet or chef cap at all times. Facial hair must be clean, well trimmed and covered with a beard net in food preparation areas.
- Shower or bathe daily before coming to work, use deodorant or antiperspirant, and maintain good oral hygiene.
- Avoid strong perfumes, colognes or scented lotions that may affect the taste of food or cause allergic reactions.

### 7.2 Uniform and appearance

- Wear the correct, full uniform for your team at all times while on duty. It must be clean, pressed and in good condition for every shift.
- Closed-toe, non-slip shoes are compulsory.
- Name tags must be worn where they can be seen.
- No caps or beanies may be worn on duty, except the navy Pelagos beanie, which may be worn when travelling to and from work and by housekeeping and maintenance staff working outside.
- Issued uniform items may not be worn off duty, except when travelling directly to and from work.

| **Team** | **Uniform** |
|---|---|
| **Front of house** | Shirt: navy button-down (long or short sleeve), tucked in and ironed. ¶ Trousers or skirt: long khaki chinos, or a knee-length khaki pencil skirt. No denim or leggings. ¶ Apron: branded apron, tied neatly and free of stains. ¶ Footwear: neat black, brown or white closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles. ¶ Grooming: long hair tied back; neat facial hair; minimal jewellery. |
| **Kitchen** | Chef jacket: standard black double-breasted jacket, clean every shift. ¶ Trousers: plain black chef trousers. ¶ Headwear: black chef skull cap. All hair must be covered. ¶ Apron: black bib apron, taken off when leaving the kitchen. ¶ Footwear: neat black closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles. |
| **Housekeeping** | Top: navy tunic. ¶ Trousers or skirt: navy trousers or knee-length pencil skirt. No denim or leggings. ¶ Footwear: neat black, brown or white closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles. ¶ Grooming: long hair tied back; minimal jewellery. |
| **Maintenance** | Top: navy overall jacket and branded T-shirt. ¶ Trousers: navy trousers. ¶ Footwear: steel-toe boots or approved safety footwear at all times. |

### If you are not in the correct uniform:

- You may be removed from the shift or sent home to change. Time away from work to fix uniform problems is unpaid.
- Arriving out of uniform repeatedly leads to disciplinary action (PEL-POL-002).
- If your uniform does not fit or is worn out, tell Management so that it can be replaced.
- Supervisors check hygiene, grooming and uniforms regularly and give feedback.

### 7.3 Wounds and illness

- Cover all cuts, burns or wounds with a waterproof plaster or dressing, and wear gloves over it when handling food.
- Report any injury to your supervisor immediately.
- If you have vomiting, diarrhoea or a fever, tell your manager before your shift. You may not handle food until you are well.
- Employees with other symptoms that may create a food safety risk must tell management and may be told not to work.

## 8. SERVICE STANDARDS

Service is the most visible part of the Pelagos brand. Food may be excellent, but poor service damages the overall guest experience. Every team member, and especially floor staff, must know and apply the Pelagos sequence of service.

### 8.1 Guest interaction

- Address guests as Mr, Mrs or Ms with their surname, or by their first name once they offer it. Do not use “ma’am”, and avoid casual language such as “guys” (see PEL-MAN-004 FOH Training Manual).
- Maintain positive body language, eye contact and a genuine smile.
- Treat guests as if they are in your own home: warmly, attentively and without annoyance.
- Never interrupt a guest. Listen fully before responding.
- Do not argue with guests or become defensive.

### 8.2 The sequence of service

1.  Greet guests promptly at the entrance or on arrival at the table.
2.  Confirm the reservation, the number of guests and any immediate needs.
3.  Lead guests confidently to their table and present clean menus.
4.  Offer beverages and, where relevant, the wine list.
5.  Take the order accurately, standing to the right of the guest where practical and serving ladies first, then gentlemen, then the host.
6.  Repeat the order back to the table and confirm all special requests, allergies and modifications.
7.  Serve beverages professionally and announce dishes when placing them down.
8.  Return within two minutes or two bites to check satisfaction.
9.  Clear quietly and professionally, usually when all guests at the table have finished the course.
10. Present the bill neatly and accurately and thank guests sincerely on departure.

### 8.3 Service language and complaint handling

- Replace “I don’t know” with “Let me find out for you.”
- Replace “We can’t” with a solution-focused alternative where possible.
- If a guest complains, apologise professionally, stay calm and involve the duty manager immediately if the matter cannot be resolved instantly.
- Do not blame the kitchen, another employee, the system or the guest.

### 8.4 Floor presence and handover

- A server must remain visible and available on the floor during service.
- Do not disappear to the kitchen, outside area or phone unless your tables have been properly covered.
- When handing over a table or ending a shift, introduce the replacement staff member to the guest where possible.

## 9. DEPARTMENTAL OPERATING STANDARDS

### 9.1 Front of house

- Open the floor correctly: wipe and set tables, prepare service stations, check menus, prepare napkins and review reservations.
- During service, monitor tables continuously, keep the floor tidy, replenish service items and communicate clearly with the kitchen and bar.
- At closing, clean all tables and chairs, switch off equipment, secure doors and windows, charge devices and leave the area reset for the next shift.

### 9.2 Bar

- Open by sanitising the bar surface, setting clean mats, preparing ice, restocking refrigerated beverages using FIFO, polishing glassware and preparing garnishes.
- During service, maintain ice, stock levels, cleanliness, garnish quality and POS functionality.
- At closing, conduct stock counts, note discrepancies, prepare a replenishment list, clean taps and surfaces, wash cloths and secure stock.

### 9.3 Deli and coffee service

- Keep all washed crockery, cutlery and utensils dry, polished and correctly stored.
- Clean the espresso machine, grinder, blender and milk jugs thoroughly every day.
- Monitor sugar caddies, condiments and slush levels and maintain clean counters and floors.
- At close, deep clean the espresso machine, power down correctly, switch equipment to the correct mode and report stock shortages.

### 9.4 Kitchen

- Follow hygiene rules, clean-as-you-go practices and correct board/utensil usage at all times.
- Label all prepared food and store it correctly in sealed containers.
- Keep raw and cooked foods separated and maintain correct storage hierarchy.
- At opening, verify cleanliness, equipment function and fridge or freezer temperatures.
- At closing, clean and sanitise all stations, equipment, floors and waste areas and secure food correctly.

### Operational non-negotiables

- All staff food and beverage consumption must be authorised and correctly recorded.
- No food may be taken from company stock without payment or written authorisation.
- Lost property and guest items must be handed to management immediately.
- Duty lists and checklists must be completed honestly and signed where required.

## 10. FOOD SAFETY, HYGIENE AND ALLERGEN CONTROL

Food safety is non-negotiable at Pelagos. Every person working around food or food-contact areas has a duty to prevent contamination, maintain hygiene and follow all legal and company procedures.

### 10.1 Core food safety controls

- Deliveries must be checked for temperature, packaging condition and suitability before they are accepted.
- FIFO must be applied at all times.
- Everything prepared or decanted must be labelled with the product name, prep date, use-by date and initials.
- Fridges must run between 0°C and 4°C and freezers at -18°C or colder.
- Poultry and pork must reach 75°C internally; fish must reach 63°C internally. Hot food kept for service must stay at 60°C or hotter.
- Thaw food in the fridge, or in a sealed bag under cold running water. Never thaw food at room temperature.
- Food may only be reheated once, to 75°C or hotter. Any leftover reheated food must be thrown away.

### 10.2 Cross-contamination and allergens

- Use correct colour-coded cutting boards and utensils.
- Store raw and cooked products separately in airtight containers.
- Clean and sanitise surfaces and equipment between tasks.
- Take all allergy information seriously. Confirm with the guest, communicate clearly to the kitchen and prevent cross-contact.

### 10.3 Cleaning, pests and records

- Surfaces, equipment, floors, drains and waste areas must be cleaned and sanitised according to schedule.
- Chemicals must be stored away from food in safe, controlled areas.
- Pest activity or signs of infestation must be reported immediately.
- Temperature logs, cleaning checklists, pest records and other food safety records must be completed accurately where required.

## 11. VILLA DEL MARE ESTATE RULES FOR STAFF

Pelagos operates within Villa Del Mare Estate. All staff must therefore comply with estate access, behaviour and security rules in addition to Pelagos rules. Estate compliance is not optional.

### 11.1 Access and registration

- Employees must be properly registered on the estate access system before access will be granted.
- Employees must use designated staff or pedestrian access points and comply with security instructions at all times.
- Valid identification and any required permit or registration details must be kept current.
- Staff may not permit unauthorised persons to access the estate or the business.

### 11.2 Movement, parking and conduct on estate

- Park only in designated staff or authorised parking areas.
- Do not park on verges, emergency zones or restricted areas.
- Be respectful to residents, estate staff, visitors and common property at all times.
- Noise, littering, vandalism, aggression or disregard for estate instructions are prohibited.
- Any suspicious behaviour, security concern or incident must be reported immediately.

### 11.3 Deliveries and contractors

- Deliveries must comply with estate access rules and may be subject to inspections.
- Only approved or authorised deliveries and service providers may enter where required.
- No staff member may override or ignore estate security procedures.

## 12. SECURITY, ASSETS AND TECHNOLOGY

### 12.1 Company property and stock

- Treat company equipment, devices, tools, furniture, vehicles and uniforms with care.
- Do not remove stock, tools, documents or company property from the premises without authorisation.
- Report damages, losses, breakages or suspicious activity immediately.
- Stock takes, requisition lists, void slips, manual sale sheets and control records must be completed honestly and accurately.

### 12.2 POS, tabs and records

- All transactions must be rung up correctly and no staff member may grant unauthorised discounts, free items or unrecorded sales.
- **Pelagos is cashless.** Staff may never accept cash from a guest, keep cash in a till or make cash payouts. If a guest offers cash, politely explain that we are cashless and offer card payment (PEL-MAN-001 Pilot POS Operating Manual, section 5).
- Where tabs are permitted, the bar procedure must be followed exactly.
- In the event of system or power failure, approved manual sale procedures must be used and captured later as directed by management.

### 12.3 Searches, alcohol and drug testing

- Employees may be subject to lawful searches of bags, personal items or vehicles when entering or leaving the premises or estate.
- The business reserves the right to conduct alcohol, drug or polygraph testing where lawful and reasonably required in an investigation.
- Being under the influence at work, possession of intoxicating substances, or refusal to comply with lawful testing procedures may result in disciplinary action.

### 12.4 Electronic communications

- Business technology is provided for work purposes.
- Passwords must be kept confidential and changed if compromised.
- Do not download, transmit or store inappropriate, unlawful or confidential material in breach of company policy.
- Management may audit company systems, devices and accounts where permitted by law.

## 13. DISCIPLINE, GRIEVANCES AND PERFORMANCE

Pelagos is committed to fair standards, fair discipline and fair opportunities to improve. Discipline exists to correct behaviour and protect the business, not simply to punish employees.

### 13.1 Discipline

- Minor or repeated misconduct may lead to verbal warnings, written warnings, final written warnings or further action depending on the seriousness of the case.
- Serious misconduct such as theft, fraud, violence, gross insubordination, serious negligence, intoxication at work or wilful damage may result in dismissal.
- Employees will be given an opportunity to state their case in disciplinary processes in line with company procedure and the law.

### 13.2 Grievances

- Employees with concerns must raise them respectfully through the correct reporting line.
- Where a grievance cannot be resolved informally, the employee may submit it in writing to management.
- Grievances must be raised professionally and not discussed with guests or external parties.

### 13.3 Performance standards

- Performance is assessed through work quality, attendance, guest interaction, teamwork, attitude, trainability, hygiene and compliance.
- Employees are expected to accept coaching, feedback and training in a professional manner.
- Repeated poor performance after support and feedback may result in incapacity management or other action.

## 14. EMERGENCY PROCEDURES

Every employee must remain calm and follow instructions in emergencies. Safety comes first. No employee may ignore or conceal incidents, injuries, hazards or emergencies.

- Medical emergency: inform management immediately, call for appropriate assistance and keep the area controlled.
- Fire emergency: raise the alarm, follow evacuation instructions and do not take unnecessary risks.
- Security incident: alert management and security immediately and do not escalate the situation through confrontation unless required for immediate safety.
- Power or water failure: follow the approved business continuity procedures and maintain food safety controls.
- Report all accidents, near misses, hazards and unsafe conditions immediately.
